_comment: Corpus for scripts/support_group_identity.py - the off-mode byte-identity gate of
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-02-support-sets-and-groups.md 3.7.
Everything here is generated by make_fixtures.py into ~1.2 KB plain 3MFs, so the corpus adds
no bulky binary data. The support configuration travels as CLI overrides rather than baked
into project files: the slicer's CLI accepts any print_config_def key as --key=value.
Two classes of input were tried and REJECTED by the plan's 5.1 experiment (same exe on both
sides of the comparison); see the Stage 2 status section:
- every .3mf under resources/handy_models/ segfaults the CLI on --slice, on an untouched
tree, with or without preset overrides. Pre-existing bug, unrelated to this work.
- resources/handy_models/OrcaToleranceTest.stl slices, but generates no support at all with
these presets AND is not self-reproducible (travel moves reorder between two runs).
- any plate holding more than one OBJECT is not self-reproducible: the print order of the
objects varies, moving whole blocks of G-code. Multi-PART objects (one object, several
MODEL_PART volumes) are reproducible, and they are what support groups are about.
common_args go on every case, and both are reproducibility requirements rather than taste -
the 5.1 experiment found each of them:
--disable-m73=1           M73 remaining-time comments are emitted when the estimate crosses
a minute boundary, and the estimate wobbles slightly between two
runs of ONE binary, shifting whole blocks of the file.
--slow-down-layer-time=0  the cooling slowdown scales feedrates by the estimated layer time,
which amplified that same wobble into differing G1 F values
(F9445 vs F9459) on small fast parts.
Neither touches geometry: every coordinate stays strictly compared.
Paths are relative to the repository root. 'args' are passed verbatim after the presets.
tree_classic was REMOVED. Classic tree support is not self-reproducible: baseline-against-
baseline on this very corpus gives 6.6% matching segments, 8 changed layers and 49 dirty
layers, run after run. Organic tree, normal supports and rafts are all stable through the
tolerance gate; only the classic tree path is not. 5.1 says to drop such a case and say so.
There is deliberately NO case here carrying support_group data. Writing a loadable multi-part
fixture by hand did not work: a plain core-spec 3MF built from <component>s imports as one
ModelObject PER component, and per-part settings keyed on either the assembly object id or the
component object id were both ignored by the importer. Until a fixture is produced BY the
slicer itself, the group round trip is covered only by the unit tests, which build multi-volume
objects with add_volume. See the Stage 2 status section.

cases.name: group_parts
cases.comment: A project whose parts carry support_group and part-level support keys, and which the SLICER ITSELF produced - see make_group_fixture.py. Stage 2's generator ignores those keys, so this case must come out exactly like the baseline, a build that does not even know support_group and drops it on load. That is the whole off-mode claim, measured. It deliberately carries no support_top_z_distance: that one ACTS in Stage 2 through the soluble rule, and a case carrying it would rightly differ.
